content.comment_body: Hello, could anyone please assist? I have six motors, each with its own hours counter, but I am unable to display them on a web-based system. I need help visualizing the counter operation as machine run hours in the web interface. Also, after powering the PLC off and on, the counter values should not reset. Any guidance, especially with an example, would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

The hours counter in [product_name] supports retention of data. To display the value in [product_name] Web Editor, you need to transfer it to the VM memory using Parameter-VM-Mapping. Navigate to Tools > Parameter-VM-Mapping. In the web editor, use the 'Scaled Time' function. Please refer to the attached example.
Hello. I'm unable to open the provided file with my web editor software, as a pop-up indicates a software update is needed. My current software version is [version_no].

I'm using the latest version of the web editor, [version_no]. Unfortunately, projects from this version cannot be opened with [version_no]. I have included screenshots of both the [product_name] program and the web editor project to help you understand the necessary steps.
You can download the upgrade for the latest version of the web editor from here: [url].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering challenges when trying to display machine run hour counters in a web-based platform, primarily due to incompatibilities between different software versions and a lack of instructions for configuring retentive counters. Users are also seeking assistance on how to correctly map PLC data to a web interface and ensure counters retain values after power cycling. Proper guidance and version alignment are needed for seamless integration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to easily visualize counter values for machine run hours on a web interface, ensure counters are retained after power cycling, and open shared example projects without version compatibility problems.
